builds.howItPlays: Each turn you pay 1 Energy and exhaust Lee Sin to give one of your cheap units a lasting +1 Might, then send it into a fight over a battlefield. You keep runes open on your opponent's turn for cheap reactions like Defy, which cancels a cheap spell, and Discipline, which gives a unit +2 Might for the turn and draws you a card.
builds.whyYou: You like starting fights early and winning them with a card your opponent didn't see coming. You enjoy ending your turn with runes still open, ready to cancel their spell or make your unit bigger in the middle of a fight. You don't mind thinking hard on both players' turns, and you'd rather win because you timed a card well than because you drew the right one. If a run of close fights sounds more fun than one big turn, this Lee Sin suits you.
builds.ratingNotes: Change 2026-09-25 (re-rate from deck picks): relabelled Midrange to Tempo and moved from 4/6.5/6.5/5 to 6/6/7/4, the mean of the style's three scored decks (tools.ts style: Tempo 6/6/7/4, mean of 3; labels Tempo, Tempo, Midrange). Pace moved by 2. The other Axes moved by 1 or less. The old numbers came from guide quotes about a Dazzling Aurora list; the new ones come from three scored tournament and Set 4 lists. deckListUrl moved from the bare /decks page to the Hartford display deck. Both old guides were dropped: they describe the Aurora/Centered shape, not this trick list. They were replaced by the three scored deck pages, fetched 2026-09-25, and none of them runs a banned card. Scored decks: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/738404f0-5ee9-4e10-851d-7a53a516f58f Hartford RQ Best of Lee Sin (Troy) Tempo 6/5.5/7/3.5; https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/bb3a1b1d-a7c2-4e8b-947d-7c3935f78cec S3RQ Vancouver Best of (TerryTheCactus) Tempo 5.5/6/7/4; https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/f1ab7deb-31c3-47bc-88e1-2a3ba00f3b9d BEST DECK LEE SIN SET 4 (Pheo) Midrange 6/6/6.5/4. Pheo's rater labelled it Midrange because it has 12 reactive cards, under the 14 Tempo needs. Adjustment (all three): complexity +1, because the Legend's buff is a 1-Energy ability to aim every turn, and Centered, Irelia and Monastery of Hirana all key off buffs. Deciding cards. Pace: 8-9 two-cost units (Irresistible Faefolk, Lonely Poro, Scuttle Crab, Pit Rookie, Legion Marauder, Mournful Witness) and 3-cost First Mate, against about six 5+ cards (Irelia, Fervent, Rengar, Trophy Hunter, Lee Sin, Centered). Stance: 20-21 bodies and 14.5-17 pressure against 10-12 answers (Defy, Sabotage, Zhonya's Hourglass, Charm, Challenge). Complexity: 12-17 reaction-speed cards (Discipline, En Garde, Defy, Zhonya's Hourglass, Ambush Nidalee and Rengar) plus the Legend's every-turn buff. Variance: no luck or swing cards, mostly full playsets, and Discipline and Scuttle Crab draw cards. No Axis on any sheet differed by 2 or more between formula and judgment. Legend ability: [1], exhaust: buff a friendly unit (a unit with no buff gets a +1 Might buff). Also played (other ways to play this Build): Wallop Sett Lee Sin https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/46f6f88c-c320-4000-b281-e7ffb27d74cf (niifty, Midrange 6/6/6.5/4; Wallop readies and Sett instead of reaction tricks); Four-Drop Lee Sin https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/9ea7471c-fabe-4c8f-8295-2f37905dbb27 (rogueafk, post-ban guide, Midrange 5/5.5/6.5/4.5; 13 four-drops, with Akshan, Mischievous stealing gear); Sona Lee Sin https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/fcbba45f-4f9e-404f-9b2d-5b6c1ba47854 (Nagy, Midrange 5/4.5/7/5; Hidden answers and rune readying into Astral Heron). Confidence: low. The bar was loosened because there are two fair decks from different authors (Troy's Hartford Best of, and TerryTheCactus's Vancouver Best of, which Four Hearts posted 2026-06-01), and every result is from before Vendetta. Reviewer check: the label is a close call. hextechanalytics calls Lee Sin combat-focused midrange, and the Set 4 list falls just short of Tempo. The LA RQ (2026-09-25 to 27) will post the first post-ban Lee Sin results, so rerun after it. The Midrange Also-played lists sit about 1 from this Build on every Axis. No written guide for the current trick list was found, so guideUrls holds only deck pages.
